# golden:  help-chat.w80
# surface: the /help command list in each session
# width:   80 columns
# palette: color
# cursor:  none
#
# Generated by go test -update-golden; do not edit by hand.
# The layout block is the render with ANSI stripped — read it for the
# columns. The ansi block is the same bytes with ESC written as ␛ — read
# it for the colour assignments. Trailing spaces are significant in both.

── layout ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
· a conversation
  commands
    /help          open the key list: every key this session answers, grouped as
                   a keybindings.toml names them and spelled the way they are
                   bound now — type to filter by key or words, [esc] or [ctrl+]]
                   closes it, and the draft is as you left it. With words after
                   it (/help keys), the whole sheet — the commands, what happens
                   mid-turn, the keys and the approval policy — is written to
                   the transcript instead
    /clear         end this session and start another (also /new)
    /paste         attach the clipboard — a screenshot, or files copied in a
                   file manager — to your next message; /paste <path> attaches a
                   file by name, /paste show <handle> opens a staged image or
                   paste full-pane, /paste drop <handle> takes one back out —
                   the handle is the one a chip leads with, Image#1, and its
                   name works too — and /paste clear drops what is staged
                   (ctrl+v). With a sentence half typed, reading mode (ctrl+o)
                   keeps it and reaches the strip of chips as its last row: ←→
                   picks a chip, enter opens it, x drops it, esc goes back to
                   the sentence; a click on a chip opens it too
    /copy [code]   copy the last response (or just its code blocks)
    /model [name]  switch the model (bare /model opens an interactive picker)
                   default [name]   show or persist the default model for new
                                    sessions
                   agents [name]    show or persist the model sub-agents run on
                                    ("inherit" follows the session model)
    /permissions   what runs without asking, and the permission mode that frames
                   it (also /perms; was /mode)
                   [name]   bare opens a picker over the five modes:
                            manual asks about every consequential call
                            accept-edits applies the edits and asks for the rest
                            auto adds the allowlist and lets the classifier
                            judge
                            read-only writes nothing — a write is refused, not
                            asked
                            plan is read-only, ending on a plan you can approve
                            here or carry into a fresh session
                   why      the latest auto-mode denial's reason
                   grants   what this session has stopped asking about
                   allow <commands|edits>   grant a whole category
                   revoke [commands|edits|hosts|agents]   take the grants back
    /reasoning     how much thinking the model does before it answers: off (the
                   default), low, medium, high, xhigh or max — ctrl+t cycles
                   them
                   [level]           set it for this session (also /think)
                   default [level]   show or persist the level new sessions
                                     start on (provider.reasoning)
    /context       the window as a meter, by category, with the tools itemised
    /stats         the session's whole bill on one screen, as the rail's SPEND
                   block reads it: the session total with the kinds of request
                   that make it up, each model's share with its own kinds and
                   what the children on it cost, each child's share by name, and
                   each turn's cost as its close row states it. [enter] on a
                   turn opens it on the turns screen. What the context window is
                   occupied by is /context. While attached to an agent, /stats
                   is that agent's own. It reads and changes nothing
    /readings      every reading the session has taken of its own run on one
                   screen, newest first: the round, the verdict, the whole
                   reading with its reason and the instruction it was judged
                   against, and whether it steered the turn and whether that
                   steer was taken back. Quiet readings are kept here too. It
                   reads and changes nothing
    /turns         every turn the session has run on one screen, newest first:
                   how it ended, its steps, tools, time and spend, what it
                   changed, its commit and its checks' verdict — the figures its
                   close row drew, beside the close itself — with the turn in
                   flight on top. [enter] opens a turn's review where it changed
                   files. A turn from an ended sitting shows its files and says
                   its figures were not kept. It reads and changes nothing
    /alerts        every alert the session has had on one screen, standing first
                   and then superseded, newest first: the command, its last
                   outcome, its runs, the turn it first broke in and what
                   answered it — a clean run or the quality gate passing, with
                   the turn. [enter] shows each run: its turn, how it ended, how
                   long it took and the evidence id its output was kept under
                   where it was cut. It reads the rail's own alerts and changes
                   nothing
    /step          open the in-flight step's card onto its calls, every call
                   with its output body, bounded; run it again to close (/ui
                   verbosity high is the same thing for every card at once)
    /status        where this session is: what it is working on, what it has
                   spent, and whether the last few turns are still on the target
                   you set it
    /sessions      the sessions running on this machine: the conversation each
                   saves to, its checkout and branch, and whether it is working
    /trust         let this checkout's own skills, agent profiles, wordings and
                   quality suites load. A clone can carry instructions, so
                   nothing of a checkout's runs until you say so; "off"
                   withdraws it and the next session starts without them
    /ui            screen density, pane layout, monochrome and mouse: /ui
                   verbosity <low|normal|high> · /ui mono <on|off> · /ui mouse
                   <on|off>
                   low draws each step's card as its header alone and leaves
                   thinking out, normal draws the header, the sentence and the
                   evidence, high opens every card onto its calls; a card you
                   opened or closed stays as you left it. The mouse is on by
                   default so the wheel scrolls the transcript, click-drag
                   selects it, and clicks open rows, open or close a card by its
                   header, or answer keys; off hands selection back to the
                   terminal, and ctrl+x flips it and saves it
                   terminal   what this terminal answered when shhh asked what
                              it can do: inline images, desktop notifications,
                              focus events, cell size
    /safety        the session's whole boundary on one screen (also /security):
                   the mode and grants, where it may write, what contains its
                   commands, the hosts it reaches, what the checkout was let
                   load, its servers, secrets and tools — each section naming
                   the command that changes it. It reads and changes nothing
    /skills        the skills this session loaded (SKILL.md directories), and
                   why any did not
    /mcp           every place this session's tools came from on one screen,
                   opened on the MCP servers: the built-in toolset, each server,
                   the language servers, the binaries found on PATH and the web
                   tools, each up or not with the tools it registered — and for
                   one that is not up, what that costs and what would move it,
                   in the words shhh mcp gives. On a server the checkout
                   declared, [a] trusts the checkout or withdraws that, after
                   asking, as /trust does; it takes effect in the next session.
                   trust <name> and distrust <name> say where that answer is
                   given
    /notes         the session's shared notebook — what the agents wrote for
                   each other, and what a backlog run wrote up, listed by
                   author. Dropping is yours alone: drop <n> removes one, clear
                   empties it
    /todo          the project's backlog: bare opens a picker · show|edit <slug>
                   · add (reads this session into proposed items you accept or
                   drop) · add <text> · block <slug> [why] · open|done|drop
                   <slug> · new <text> · groom <slug> (reads an item against the
                   tree and proposes the corrections) · run [slug|--next] works
                   an item through its profile's run · sprint · status · stop
    /compact       continue from a summary plus the most recent turns
    /rewind [n]    rewind to the end of turn [n], 0 being the start (bare
                   /rewind picks interactively); the abandoned tail is kept as a
                   branch, and a card asks whether the files come back too
    /suggest       ask the suggestion model for a next step from what the last
                   turn left (also /suggestion). The answer stands dim in the
                   empty draft and → takes it, as an offer after a turn does; it
                   works whether /ui suggest is on or off, and a second ask
                   replaces the first. /ui suggest <on|off> stays the switch for
                   the offer after each turn
    /exit          quit (also /quit, /q)

· a coding session
  commands
    /help          open the key list: every key this session answers, grouped as
                   a keybindings.toml names them and spelled the way they are
                   bound now — type to filter by key or words, [esc] or [ctrl+]]
                   closes it, and the draft is as you left it. With words after
                   it (/help keys), the whole sheet — the commands, what happens
                   mid-turn, the keys and the approval policy — is written to
                   the transcript instead
    /clear         end this session and start another (also /new)
    /paste         attach the clipboard — a screenshot, or files copied in a
                   file manager — to your next message; /paste <path> attaches a
                   file by name, /paste show <handle> opens a staged image or
                   paste full-pane, /paste drop <handle> takes one back out —
                   the handle is the one a chip leads with, Image#1, and its
                   name works too — and /paste clear drops what is staged
                   (ctrl+v). With a sentence half typed, reading mode (ctrl+o)
                   keeps it and reaches the strip of chips as its last row: ←→
                   picks a chip, enter opens it, x drops it, esc goes back to
                   the sentence; a click on a chip opens it too
    /copy [code]   copy the last response (or just its code blocks)
    /model [name]  switch the model (bare /model opens an interactive picker)
                   default [name]   show or persist the default model for new
                                    sessions
                   agents [name]    show or persist the model sub-agents run on
                                    ("inherit" follows the session model)
    /permissions   what runs without asking, and the permission mode that frames
                   it (also /perms; was /mode)
                   [name]   bare opens a picker over the five modes:
                            manual asks about every consequential call
                            accept-edits applies the edits and asks for the rest
                            auto adds the allowlist and lets the classifier
                            judge
                            read-only writes nothing — a write is refused, not
                            asked

                            here or carry into a fresh session
                   why      the latest auto-mode denial's reason
                   grants   what this session has stopped asking about
                   allow <commands|edits>   grant a whole category
                   revoke [commands|edits|hosts|agents]   take the grants back
    /reasoning     how much thinking the model does before it answers: off (the
                   default), low, medium, high, xhigh or max — ctrl+t cycles
                   them
                   [level]           set it for this session (also /think)
                   default [level]   show or persist the level new sessions
                                     start on (provider.reasoning)
    /context       the window as a meter, by category, with the tools itemised
    /stats         the session's whole bill on one screen, as the rail's SPEND
                   block reads it: the session total with the kinds of request
                   that make it up, each model's share with its own kinds and
                   what the children on it cost, each child's share by name, and
                   each turn's cost as its close row states it. [enter] on a
                   turn opens it on the turns screen. What the context window is
                   occupied by is /context. While attached to an agent, /stats
                   is that agent's own. It reads and changes nothing
    /readings      every reading the session has taken of its own run on one
                   screen, newest first: the round, the verdict, the whole
                   reading with its reason and the instruction it was judged
                   against, and whether it steered the turn and whether that
                   steer was taken back. Quiet readings are kept here too. It
                   reads and changes nothing
    /turns         every turn the session has run on one screen, newest first:
                   how it ended, its steps, tools, time and spend, what it
                   changed, its commit and its checks' verdict — the figures its
                   close row drew, beside the close itself — with the turn in
                   flight on top. [enter] opens a turn's review where it changed
                   files. A turn from an ended sitting shows its files and says
                   its figures were not kept. It reads and changes nothing
    /alerts        every alert the session has had on one screen, standing first
                   and then superseded, newest first: the command, its last
                   outcome, its runs, the turn it first broke in and what
                   answered it — a clean run or the quality gate passing, with
                   the turn. [enter] shows each run: its turn, how it ended, how
                   long it took and the evidence id its output was kept under
                   where it was cut. It reads the rail's own alerts and changes
                   nothing
    /step          open the in-flight step's card onto its calls, every call
                   with its output body, bounded; run it again to close (/ui
                   verbosity high is the same thing for every card at once)
    /steps         the session's own working list on one screen: every step it
                   declared, the paths each said it would touch, which it has
                   marked done and the one it is on — and beside each, the calls
                   the transcript titled for it, or not started where there are
                   none. It reads and changes nothing
    /status        where this session is: what it is working on, what it has
                   spent, and whether the last few turns are still on the target
                   you set it
    /sessions      the sessions running on this machine: the conversation each
                   saves to, its checkout and branch, and whether it is working
    /trust         let this checkout's own skills, agent profiles, wordings and
                   quality suites load. A clone can carry instructions, so
                   nothing of a checkout's runs until you say so; "off"
                   withdraws it and the next session starts without them
    /ui            screen density, pane layout, monochrome and mouse: /ui
                   verbosity <low|normal|high> · /ui mono <on|off> · /ui mouse
                   <on|off>
                   low draws each step's card as its header alone and leaves
                   thinking out, normal draws the header, the sentence and the
                   evidence, high opens every card onto its calls; a card you
                   opened or closed stays as you left it. The mouse is on by
                   default so the wheel scrolls the transcript, click-drag
                   selects it, and clicks open rows, open or close a card by its
                   header, or answer keys; off hands selection back to the
                   terminal, and ctrl+x flips it and saves it
                   terminal   what this terminal answered when shhh asked what
                              it can do: inline images, desktop notifications,
                              focus events, cell size
    /sandbox       containment status and container sandboxes
                   (doctor|scope|list|status|destroy <id>|prune)
    /safety        the session's whole boundary on one screen (also /security):
                   the mode and grants, where it may write, what contains its
                   commands, the hosts it reaches, what the checkout was let
                   load, its servers, secrets and tools — each section naming
                   the command that changes it. It reads and changes nothing
    /skills        the skills this session loaded (SKILL.md directories), and
                   why any did not
    /mcp           every place this session's tools came from on one screen,
                   opened on the MCP servers: the built-in toolset, each server,
                   the language servers, the binaries found on PATH and the web
                   tools, each up or not with the tools it registered — and for
                   one that is not up, what that costs and what would move it,
                   in the words shhh mcp gives. On a server the checkout
                   declared, [a] trusts the checkout or withdraws that, after
                   asking, as /trust does; it takes effect in the next session.
                   trust <name> and distrust <name> say where that answer is
                   given
    /notes         the session's shared notebook — what the agents wrote for
                   each other, and what a backlog run wrote up, listed by
                   author. Dropping is yours alone: drop <n> removes one, clear
                   empties it
    /todo          the project's backlog: bare opens a picker · show|edit <slug>
                   · add (reads this session into proposed items you accept or
                   drop) · add <text> · block <slug> [why] · open|done|drop
                   <slug> · new <text> · groom <slug> (reads an item against the
                   tree and proposes the corrections) · run [slug|--next] works
                   an item through its profile's run · sprint · status · stop
    /plan          the approved plan as a checklist on the steps screen — each
                   step, the paths it named, its state and the calls that
                   carried it out — with anything that has departed from it ·
                   save [name] writes the last plan/response to .shhh/plans/ ·
                   drop forgets an approved plan
    /edit <path>   open a file in a pane over the feed and edit it yourself:
                   every key types, [ctrl+s] saves through the same write the
                   agent's edits take, so the turn's close counts it as changed
                   by you and /undo reaches it, and [esc] goes back to the
                   prompt — asking first if the buffer differs from the disk. A
                   file outside the working scope is refused; /add-dir brings
                   its directory in
    /diff [path]   show what this session changed, full screen, or one file's —
                   read from the session's own changeset, so it works outside a
                   git repository
    /review [turn] review what a turn changed: file list, hunks and the turn's
                   verdict (bare reviews the last turn that changed anything).
                   Also a turn's changed-files row, clicked or selected and
                   opened with enter. It reads and changes nothing; /undo takes
                   a turn back
    /undo [turn]   put back what a turn changed, from the session's own records
                   (not git). Asks first, names anything that changed since, and
                   is itself recorded as a turn
    /compact       continue from a summary plus the most recent turns
    /rewind [n]    rewind to the end of turn [n], 0 being the start (bare
                   /rewind picks interactively); the abandoned tail is kept as a
                   branch, and a card asks whether the files come back too
    /suggest       ask the suggestion model for a next step from what the last
                   turn left (also /suggestion). The answer stands dim in the
                   empty draft and → takes it, as an offer after a turn does; it
                   works whether /ui suggest is on or off, and a second ask
                   replaces the first. /ui suggest <on|off> stays the switch for
                   the offer after each turn
    /exit          quit (also /quit, /q)

                   ␛[38;5;245m<on|off>␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mlow draws each step's card as its header alone and leaves␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthinking out, normal draws the header, the sentence and the␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mevidence, high opens every card onto its calls; a card you␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mopened or closed stays as you left it. The mouse is on by␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mdefault so the wheel scrolls the transcript, click-drag␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mselects it, and clicks open rows, open or close a card by its␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mheader, or answer keys; off hands selection back to the␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mterminal, and ctrl+x flips it and saves it␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mterminal   what this terminal answered when shhh asked what␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m           it can do: inline images, desktop notifications,␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m           focus events, cell size␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/safety␛[m        ␛[38;5;245mthe session's whole boundary on one screen (also /security):␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthe mode and grants, where it may write, what contains its␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mcommands, the hosts it reaches, what the checkout was let␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mload, its servers, secrets and tools — each section naming␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthe command that changes it. It reads and changes nothing␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/skills␛[m        ␛[38;5;245mthe skills this session loaded (SKILL.md directories), and␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mwhy any did not␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/mcp␛[m           ␛[38;5;245mevery place this session's tools came from on one screen,␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mopened on the MCP servers: the built-in toolset, each server,␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthe language servers, the binaries found on PATH and the web␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mtools, each up or not with the tools it registered — and for␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mone that is not up, what that costs and what would move it,␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245min the words shhh mcp gives. On a server the checkout␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mdeclared, [a] trusts the checkout or withdraws that, after␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245masking, as /trust does; it takes effect in the next session.␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mtrust <name> and distrust <name> say where that answer is␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mgiven␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/notes␛[m         ␛[38;5;245mthe session's shared notebook — what the agents wrote for␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245meach other, and what a backlog run wrote up, listed by␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mauthor. Dropping is yours alone: drop <n> removes one, clear␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mempties it␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/todo␛[m          ␛[38;5;245mthe project's backlog: bare opens a picker · show|edit <slug>␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m· add (reads this session into proposed items you accept or␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mdrop) · add <text> · block <slug> [why] · open|done|drop␛[m

                   ␛[38;5;245man item through its profile's run · sprint · status · stop␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/compact␛[m       ␛[38;5;245mcontinue from a summary plus the most recent turns␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/rewind [n]␛[m    ␛[38;5;245mrewind to the end of turn [n], 0 being the start (bare␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m/rewind picks interactively); the abandoned tail is kept as a␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mbranch, and a card asks whether the files come back too␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/suggest␛[m       ␛[38;5;245mask the suggestion model for a next step from what the last␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mturn left (also /suggestion). The answer stands dim in the␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mempty draft and → takes it, as an offer after a turn does; it␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mworks whether /ui suggest is on or off, and a second ask␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mreplaces the first. /ui suggest <on|off> stays the switch for␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthe offer after each turn␛[m

· a coding session
  ␛[38;5;246mcommands␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/help␛[m          ␛[38;5;245mopen the key list: every key this session answers, grouped as␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245ma keybindings.toml names them and spelled the way they are␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mbound now — type to filter by key or words, [esc] or [ctrl+]]␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mcloses it, and the draft is as you left it. With words after␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mit (/help keys), the whole sheet — the commands, what happens␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mmid-turn, the keys and the approval policy — is written to␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthe transcript instead␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/clear␛[m         ␛[38;5;245mend this session and start another (also /new)␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/paste␛[m         ␛[38;5;245mattach the clipboard — a screenshot, or files copied in a␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mfile manager — to your next message; /paste <path> attaches a␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mfile by name, /paste show <handle> opens a staged image or␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mpaste full-pane, /paste drop <handle> takes one back out —␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthe handle is the one a chip leads with, Image#1, and its␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mname works too — and /paste clear drops what is staged␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m(ctrl+v). With a sentence half typed, reading mode (ctrl+o)␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mkeeps it and reaches the strip of chips as its last row: ←→␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mpicks a chip, enter opens it, x drops it, esc goes back to␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthe sentence; a click on a chip opens it too␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/copy [code]␛[m   ␛[38;5;245mcopy the last response (or just its code blocks)␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/model [name]␛[m  ␛[38;5;245mswitch the model (bare /model opens an interactive picker)␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mdefault [name]   show or persist the default model for new␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m                 sessions␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245magents [name]    show or persist the model sub-agents run on␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m                 ("inherit" follows the session model)␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/permissions␛[m   ␛[38;5;245mwhat runs without asking, and the permission mode that frames␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mit (also /perms; was /mode)␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m[name]   bare opens a picker over the five modes:␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m         manual asks about every consequential call␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m         accept-edits applies the edits and asks for the rest␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m         auto adds the allowlist and lets the classifier␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m         judge␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m         read-only writes nothing — a write is refused, not␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m         asked␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m         plan is read-only, ending on a plan you can approve␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m         here or carry into a fresh session␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mwhy      the latest auto-mode denial's reason␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mgrants   what this session has stopped asking about␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mallow <commands|edits>   grant a whole category␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mrevoke [commands|edits|hosts|agents]   take the grants back␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/reasoning␛[m     ␛[38;5;245mhow much thinking the model does before it answers: off (the␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mdefault), low, medium, high, xhigh or max — ctrl+t cycles␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthem␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m[level]           set it for this session (also /think)␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mdefault [level]   show or persist the level new sessions␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245m                  start on (provider.reasoning)␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/context␛[m       ␛[38;5;245mthe window as a meter, by category, with the tools itemised␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/stats␛[m         ␛[38;5;245mthe session's whole bill on one screen, as the rail's SPEND␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mblock reads it: the session total with the kinds of request␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthat make it up, each model's share with its own kinds and␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mwhat the children on it cost, each child's share by name, and␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245meach turn's cost as its close row states it. [enter] on a␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mturn opens it on the turns screen. What the context window is␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245moccupied by is /context. While attached to an agent, /stats␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mis that agent's own. It reads and changes nothing␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/readings␛[m      ␛[38;5;245mevery reading the session has taken of its own run on one␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mscreen, newest first: the round, the verdict, the whole␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mreading with its reason and the instruction it was judged␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245magainst, and whether it steered the turn and whether that␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245msteer was taken back. Quiet readings are kept here too. It␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mreads and changes nothing␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/turns␛[m         ␛[38;5;245mevery turn the session has run on one screen, newest first:␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mhow it ended, its steps, tools, time and spend, what it␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mchanged, its commit and its checks' verdict — the figures its␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mclose row drew, beside the close itself — with the turn in␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mflight on top. [enter] opens a turn's review where it changed␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mfiles. A turn from an ended sitting shows its files and says␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mits figures were not kept. It reads and changes nothing␛[m
    ␛[38;5;252m/alerts␛[m        ␛[38;5;245mevery alert the session has had on one screen, standing first␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mand then superseded, newest first: the command, its last␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245moutcome, its runs, the turn it first broke in and what␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245manswered it — a clean run or the quality gate passing, with␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mthe turn. [enter] shows each run: its turn, how it ended, how␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;245mlong it took and the evidence id its output was kept under␛[m
